result.name: Tutorial — Your First Company
result.description: Learn the core loop in Metropolis: open a supermarket, stock it with imported soft drinks, and watch the first months' books. Imported goods bought at world prices leave a thin margin; advertising, a second product line and a well-judged bank loan are the levers that turn a small store into a growing company. There is no deadline, and the advisor (H) walks you through every step.
goals: Open your first store. Press B to open Build, pick Retail › Supermarket and place it on a busy street in Metropolis — high-traffic plots bring more shoppers. Building costs cash up front and the store becomes an asset on your balance sheet.

Stock soft drinks. Click your supermarket to open its inspector, add a Soft Drink line and keep the price near the suggested band (around $1.65 a bottle, a little under the going rate). The store buys its stock from the world market automatically.

Earn a profitable month. Let time run (Space, or 1–4 for speed) and read the month-close summary. Imported soft drinks leave a thin margin after wages, running costs and depreciation — that is normal, and the next steps show how to widen it.

Advertise. Open Marketing (K) and start a TV campaign for soft drinks in Metropolis. Brand awareness lets you sell more at a better price; the forecast shows how quickly it builds and how fast it fades if you stop paying.
Reach 30 brand awareness for soft drinks in Metropolis. Keep the campaign running in the city where you actually sell — brand only pays where your shelves are.

Borrow to grow. Open Finance (F) › Bank and take a term loan sized to your next investment. The offer shows the rate your credit rating earns, the monthly payment, and the interest that will appear below operating profit in your income statement.
Add a second product line. Use the loan to put bread on a free unit of your supermarket (or open a second store). More lines spread the store's fixed costs over more sales.

Grow company value to $55M. Company value prices your business on its earnings: cash counts at face value, and stores are worth more than their cost only when they earn more than investors require. Check the Reports (R) balance sheet and income statement to see what moves it.

result.name: Export Tycoon
result.description: You start with a modest treasury and a mandate to conquer the world market. Stand up farms and factories, sell their output abroad, and earn $125M of export revenue inside five years. The world market is deep but not bottomless: every extra unit you export fetches a little less.
goals: Earn $125M of export revenue in total within five years — about two well-run export lines. Turn on export for a factory in its inspector.

result.name: Tech Titan Clash
result.description: A premium-brand rival with twice your capital is flooding the high-income aisles with flagship televisions and cars, priced well above the market. Out-engineer them in the Eastside car market, out-sell them on Metropolis televisions, and still be standing — and worth more — when the five years are up.
goals: Sell 30% of the cars bought in Eastside (trailing three months) — the rival's first stronghold.
Sell 25% of the televisions bought in Metropolis — deny the titan a clean sweep of the densest market.
Be worth at least $125M when the scenario ends in December 2030 — survive the spending war and come out ahead.

Top the brand charts in soft drinks and cars, grind out 18 profitable months in a row, and still be worth $100M when the seven years are up.
